summary: Fifty seconds of budget remain, which is not enough for another patch cycle, so I am returning the retained draft unchanged: it is the revision accepted last turn, which anchored the documented purpose of LeadershipTransferToServer alongside its code, matching the anchoring the verification finding received before it. The record ends here, and what it holds is this. The captured tree matches the released upstream copy of the same revision byte for byte, so nothing found is injected. The most severe result is the durable term regression, witnessed twice with a causal control separating it from the instrumentation and bounded by two uninstrumented probes at zero falls in 792 and 768 deliveries, with the remaining uncertainty stated precisely as application order at the shared store key rather than latency, and the discriminating test named for a successor. Also witnessed: an explicit transfer to a member holding no vote reported as success while moving authority nowhere; the AddVoter documentation promising a staging phase the implementation never enters, shown end to end with a control; an accepted apply or barrier duty with no completion path after shutdown; and the configuration index handed to callers as a constant zero that disables the documented compare-and-swap precondition. Settled by reading with scopes: the heartbeat fast path bypasses the protocol gate every other RPC path enforces, and the leader verification counts acknowledgements from members outside the voter set it targets, which an audit confirms is the only such count in the package. Each of those now carries both halves of its comparison, the documented promise and the code. Negative results are recorded wherever a suspicion did not survive - the log cache under in-tree producers, the commit index arithmetic, the bootstrap term write, the heartbeat release path - and the corrections keep earlier phrasing inside what the evidence supports rather than letting it drift.
